chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Tap dancing as the vanishing bachelor
summary: Green compares tap to a rare bachelor hunted by Frank Buck, and the woman interviewer concludes tap was the thing people looked for and could not find.

blocks.x: Well, what was happening to the performers and the --

I mean, they didn't see it -- it seemed to be going away just like if a hunter was go way out in the woods, you know, or deep in the forest or in the jungles, you know, and he's looking for a certain kind of -- what do they
call them? A baron -- you know, like a single person -- a single man, you know -- what do they call that?

A single man?
Bachelor -- bachelor, see, now, he could pass by all kinds of -- you know, pedigrees of animals or species, you know, but they only want the bachelors, you see. They want to get the certain kind of bachelor, you see. Like what they call the king of the jungle, you know. Who was it went out there -- Frank and Buck -- Frank Buck and his wife -- Mr. and Mrs. Frank Buck -- right? Bring them back alive, you see. That's what they used to do. They used to go out in Clyde Beatty, you see -- he had, I think, some bachelors, you see. They're very rare, you see -- bachelors. Don't laugh, don't laugh. I know you're very inquisitive and interested in the contents that's going to be introduced, but this is for a great day in the history of America, which they call the land of the free and the home of the brave, you see. Are you trying to say that tap dancing was the bachelor that one was looking for and couldn't find?
